title: The ship you keep repairing
dek: If every plank is replaced, is it still the same ship — and are you still the same person who started the week?
speakingPrompts: Explain the Ship of Theseus to someone using a house, a band, or a football club instead of a ship.
Are you the same person you were at sixteen? Give your answer in two minutes without hiding in poetry.
If a company replaces every founder, office, and product, what, if anything, still deserves the original name?

blocks.text: Plutarch tells of the ship of Theseus, maintained by the Athenians: planks rot, planks are swapped, and a question appears that will not rot with them. If no original timber remains, is it the same ship? Thomas Hobbes later added a second vessel built from the discarded planks. Now there are two candidates for identity. Our intuitions split, which is the point.

One family of answers cares about continuity of form and function: it is the same ship if it has been one maintained object, even if its matter changed. Another cares about material: identity tracks the wood. A third treats the puzzle as a reminder that “same” is a word with jobs. We use it for legal ownership, for sentimental attachment, for physical composition, and those jobs do not always vote together.

You already live inside a version of this. Cells turn over. Preferences migrate. The name on your documents stays. Memory claims to be the keel — except memory, as Curio’s psychology shelf argues, is itself repaired and sometimes invented. If identity requires an unbroken inner recording, we are all in trouble. If it requires a practical, socially recognised continuity, we are mostly fine, and the puzzle becomes a tool for noticing which kind of sameness we are asking for.
We are not statues. We are maintenance.
blocks.cite: A working line, not a quotation from Plutarch

blocks.text: What to do with the splinter

Thought experiments earn their keep when they change a decision. If you are restoring a building, do you owe more to the façade or the use? If a band keeps the name after every original member has left, who is being misled? If you have changed, which promises still bind you? The ship does not need a single metaphysical verdict to be useful. It needs you to say, in each case, which sense of “same” you are willing to defend out loud.
